title: Potato Biology Notes for Potatoism

notes.biology: Potato tubers can remain dormant before they sprout.
notes.practice_reflection: Not every quiet period is failure. Some phases are for storage and preparation.

notes.biology: A young potato may have one dominant eye while other eyes remain inactive.
notes.practice_reflection: Early growth may need one clear direction before many branches are useful.

notes.biology: Older seed potatoes can activate more eyes and produce more stems.
notes.practice_reflection: Greater maturity can support more simultaneous paths without losing the original root.

notes.biology: A seed potato piece needs a viable eye or bud to begin new growth.
notes.practice_reflection: A new branch needs a real point of future action, not merely separation from the old one.

notes.biology: Potato tubers store energy that supports later sprouting.
notes.practice_reflection: Learning, rest, savings and memory can be stored capacity for future action.

notes.biology: Sprouting timing depends on age, variety and environment.
notes.practice_reflection: Growth should not be forced into one universal timetable.

rule: Keep biological fact and philosophical interpretation separate, then use the comparison only when it remains useful.
